title: Restore falls back to base on any branch-fetch failure, then force-push wipes it
description:
restoreWorkspace treats any non-zero exit of 'git fetch origin $BRANCH' as 'the branch does not exist yet' and restores at the base. That includes a forge 5xx, a network blip or a token-door hiccup. The next round's pushWipCheckpoint does 'git push -f' to the attempt branch, overwriting every earlier wip snapshot and the agent's commits. A transient failure during a restore therefore silently loses the attempt's work. Distinguish a missing ref (git ls-remote) from a failed fetch, and fail the restore on the latter.
